overview.text: Gian Lorenzo Bernini (1598–1680) was an Italian sculptor, architect, painter, and designer whose career centered on Rome, where popes and cardinals helped make him a leading artist of the Baroque. His lively figures, with twisting poses, expressive faces, and flowing drapery, make marble seem animated. He also combined sculpture, architecture, and theatrical effects to create unified settings. In the Cornaro Chapel, The Ecstasy of Saint Teresa presents a religious vision within a setting of colored marble and architecture. In Piazza Navona, his Fountain of the Four Rivers groups allegorical river figures around a basin and obelisk. Bernini also shaped the approach to St Peter’s with a monumental colonnade.

key_facts.text: Bernini was born in Naples in 1598 and trained in the workshop of his father, sculptor Pietro Bernini.
His sculptures for Cardinal Scipione Borghese helped establish him as a leading sculptor in Italy.
The Ecstasy of Saint Teresa (1647–52) is part of the Cornaro Chapel in Rome; Bernini integrated the sculpture with architecture and colored marble.
The Fountain of the Four Rivers in Piazza Navona places personifications of four rivers around a basin, with an obelisk above them.
Bernini designed the colonnade in front of St Peter’s, transforming the approach to the church.
